set_text.text: Product pricing is choosing what a case sells for. The price has to clear what the case costs you and stay close to what the account could pay elsewhere. For a distributor, a pricing rule decides where in that range each case lands.
Nothing sells below landed cost for long. In the calculator's example the floor is $22.00 a case, and every rule's margin is measured from it.
The ceiling is the account's other option
A competitor at $31.00 sets the price your account compares you against. Reliable delivery can stretch that ceiling a little, not remove it.
The rule picks a spot in between
Here the room between cost and the market is $9.00 a case. The rule you choose decides how much of it you keep and how much you give up to hold the account.
Who uses a product pricing calculator
It is built for independent food distributors who set their own prices. Anyone who quotes a case, answers a rival quote or adds a new line should run it before the price goes out.
